features.summary: Execution: how a plan runs in the browser. Boot starts each owner's handlers in plan order; a handler runs one run, a state machine whose steps run in the trigger's turn until one awaits, and only the closed awaited steps C# marks wait: a send, a Confirm, a hub's invoke and send, and a method declared MethodAsync, whose rejection stops the run. Steps before the first await run in the vendor's turn, so a payload write there reaches the vendor, and C# refuses one after it on the path the handler runs. A stop unwinds the run's frames innermost first, each request running its Finally layers once; a replace or a dispose aborts the run's blocks and runs no route; a join waits for every block's tail. Data read where a member is absent reads the start System.Text.Json binds for it, stops where the binding cannot make the holder or the holder lacks what its type requires, and a path value that reads nothing stops its request before it is sent. Main drops a call's promise and refuses no late payload write; the redesign logs a rejection and goes on, reads data's members as optional, and ends no run at dispose.

sentences.text: Pure sync reactions must return before Syncfusion inspects mutable event args
Two-phase wiring: wire all non-page-ready listeners first, then execute page-ready.
if (isPromise(completion)) return completion.then(() => runFrom(statements, index + 1, scope));
objects.subscribe(handler.on, handler.path, handler.event, payload => runHandler(handler, payload, objects), owner);
if (isMissing(value)) throw new Error(`[alis] route param "${name}" evaluated to null; cannot build URL`);
G.Let(response, G.Call(G.Obj(scope.Objects.Http()), PathMembers.Required, "send", SendArgument(method, input, scope)), awaits: true),

A pipeline runs as one run, a state machine whose driver alone continues on a promise: its steps run in the trigger's turn until one awaits, a stop unwinds its frames innermost first, running each request's Finally layers, and ends its own handler only.
A write to the trigger's payload itself after an awaited step, on the path the handler runs, is refused where the view renders, and a write to an object the payload holds runs.

A handler's policy, overlap, replace or skip, decides what a trigger does while its run is in flight; replace and a dispose abort the run's blocks' signals, and each Finally layer whose WhileLoading completed runs once.

features.oracle: The spec itself where the framework is the authority: spec/Execution/Run.tla, Lanes.tla and Absence.tla, whose invariants TLC checks, and Request.tla's states, which Run.tla runs as frames; ECMA-262's promise jobs for what runs in a turn; the DOM and Fetch Standards' AbortSignal and fetch, pinned in spec/probes (abort-signal-keeps-first-reason, fetch-aborted-signal-sends-nothing); System.Text.Json 10's binding for a data member's start (core-stj-empty-object-start, core-stj-populate-start, core-json-nested-start); and EJ2 33.1.47's declared return types and payloads (ej2-methods-returning-promise, ej2-filtering-args-members).

promises.page: The admission screen, whose Find a free bed button sends GET /beds/free, which answers {"bed": null} when the ward is full; its success route sends GET /beds/{bedId} with bedId read from the answer's Bed.Id. That second request's WhileLoading writes Opening into bed-status, its busy indicator is bed-busy, its success route writes the bed's name into bed-name and its Finally writes Closed into bed-status.

promises.outcome: bed-status reads Closed, bed-busy never shows, bed-name stays empty, and only the GET /beds/free request is sent.
promises.opposite: With bed East 4 free, the same click shows bed-busy while the second request is in flight, then East 4 in bed-name and Closed in bed-status.
promises.defect: The missing path value throws inside the send, as the redesign's route fill does (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/plugins/http.ts:83 at 65fdf118d), so the Finally never runs and bed-status keeps Opening; or the request is sent with an empty segment and its answer shows in bed-name.

promises.page: The bench page on an app whose JSON options write under WhenWritingDefault, with the ConformanceComponent conformance, whose Bindings hold three bindings as data those options wrote and whose Binding holds a binding whose data lacks started. Binding declares Count, an int, and Started, a string initialized to start. Alpha's count is 0 and its started own, Beta's count is 0 and its started null, so Beta's data holds neither, and Gamma's count is 2 and its started start. Count the zero counts writes the count of bindings whose Count is 0 into zero-count; Count the started writes the count of bindings whose Started is start into started-count; Show Beta's started writes the Started of the binding Find(b => b.Name == "Beta") returns into beta-started; Show the binding's started writes Binding's Started into binding-started.
promises.gesture: Click Count the zero counts, Count the started, Show Beta's started and Show the binding's started.
promises.outcome: zero-count reads 2, started-count reads 2, beta-started reads start and binding-started reads start.
promises.opposite: With Beta's count 1 and its started other, zero-count reads 1, started-count reads 1 and beta-started reads other; with the Binding's data holding started bound, binding-started reads bound.
promises.defect: An absent member reads nothing, as the redesign reads data's members as optional (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Values/Target.cs:80 at 65fdf118d), so zero-count reads 0, started-count reads 1, and beta-started and binding-started stay empty; or the browser picks a start by the member's shape, so beta-started shows an empty text.

promises.defect: One start per type, as the redesign builds a start from the type alone (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Validation/ModelDefaults.cs:126 at 65fdf118d), so all three read own start; or an absent member reads nothing and the three stay empty.

promises.page: The bench page on an app whose JSON options set RespectRequiredConstructorParameters, with the ConformanceComponent conformance, whose Binding is a record whose constructor takes Name and Code: Beta's data lacks code, and Gamma's holds both and lacks count. promises.page: The bench page. The ConformanceComponent conformance declares Settle() as a MethodAsync that awaits the test app's settle endpoint, SettleRecord() as a MethodAsync<Record> that answers the record endpoint's record, of count 125 and code C-750, SettleMaybe() as a MethodAsync<Record?> that answers nothing, and TakeText(Arg<string?> text), a method that shows the text it receives as its taken text, (null) when it receives null; conformance-older, of the older version, declares SettleRecord() the same way while its method returns a plain record of count 90. Run the self-test writes Testing into check-status, awaits Settle() and writes Self-test passed; Read the count writes the record's Count into record-count; Show the remote code writes the record's Code into record-code; Read older's count writes conformance-older's record's Count into older-count; Take the missing record passes SettleMaybe()'s Name to TakeText. The harness seeds the settle endpoint's answers, a success and then a 500, and gates each (Run.tla's Settle); Settle() rejects when the endpoint answers a 500.
promises.gesture: Click Run the self-test and, once the harness reports the settle held, release it, the endpoint answering the seeded success; click Run the self-test again and, once held, release it, the endpoint answering the seeded 500; then click Read the count, Show the remote code, Read older's count and Take the missing record.
promises.outcome: check-status reads Testing until the first release and Self-test passed after it; after the second run and the 500 it reads Testing; record-count reads 125, record-code C-750, older-count 90, and conformance's taken text (null).
promises.opposite: Before the first release, check-status keeps Testing; with the record endpoint answering a count of 60, record-count reads 60.
promises.defect: The step after the call runs in the call's turn, as main drops a call's promise (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/execution/reactions/execute.ts:181 at 623dd4a27), so Self-test passed shows before the release and after the 500; or a resolution to nothing reaches TakeText as undefined, which shows (undefined); or the older version's plain value stops the pipeline, so older-count stays empty.

The drawer's BeforeClose handler, when ClosedBy is the close button, writes the event's Cancel, then asks with Confirm "Discard the unsaved care plan?" and, on Yes, calls the drawer's Close, whose own BeforeClose writes no Cancel.

promises.opposite: With the settle endpoint seeded to answer a success, settle-status reads Settled after the release, order-status reads Finished and order-busy hides.

promises.page: The resident record's care panel, a ConformanceComponent whose Raise button raises Raised with its outer object, a live object whose text the panel shows as Outer: Gamma. The Raised handler awaits the care panel's Settle(), which awaits the test app's settle endpoint, then writes acknowledged into the payload's Outer.Text. The harness gates the settle endpoint (Run.tla's Settle).

promises.page: Three care panels, each a ConformanceComponent on the resident record that raises Raised from its own Raise button and, once its listeners return, shows its payload line, Payload text: and what its handlers wrote into the payload's WriteOnlyText, or none, then counts the payload's total down from 3 to 2. The first panel's handler writes Kappa into the payload's WriteOnlyText and Writing into ack-status, awaits the panel's Settle(), which awaits the test app's settle endpoint, then writes acknowledged into the payload's Outer.Text, calls the payload's Act(), which the panel shows as Payload acted, and writes the payload's Total() and Settled into ack-total and ack-status. The second panel has two handlers: the first awaits its panel's Settle() at once, and the second, written after it, writes Kappa into the payload's WriteOnlyText before its own await. The third panel's handler writes nothing to its payload. The harness gates the settle endpoint (Run.tla's Settle).
promises.gesture: Click Raise on each panel; once the harness reports the first panel's settle held, check the panels, then release it.
promises.outcome: The first panel shows Payload text: Kappa and ack-status reads Writing; after the release its outer reads acknowledged, it shows Payload acted, ack-total reads 2 and ack-status reads Settled; the second panel shows Payload text: Kappa and the third Payload text: none.
promises.opposite: Before the release, the first panel's outer reads Gamma, it shows no Payload acted line and ack-total stays empty.
promises.defect: The handler continues after a microtask, so the first panel reads no write and shows Payload text: none; or the second handler waits for the first one's await, so its write misses the second panel's turn and it shows Payload text: none; or a read after the await reads a snapshot of the payload, so ack-total reads 3.

promises.page: The resident record's care panel, a ConformanceComponent whose Raised handler, when the payload's Flag holds, awaits the panel's Settle(), which awaits the test app's settle endpoint, which answers at once, and in its Else writes Kappa into the payload's WriteOnlyText; once its listeners return the panel shows its payload line, Payload text: Kappa or Payload text: none. Its Raise flagged and Raise unflagged buttons raise Raised with Flag true and false. On the resident record, the link Late write opens a page whose handler writes the WriteOnlyText after that When.

promises.defect: The C# counts any await in the handler as before every write, so the first page is refused; or the Else runs after the panel's turn, so Raise unflagged shows Payload text: none; or the late write passes the render and reaches no vendor.

promises.page: The resident record's care panel, a ConformanceComponent whose Raised handler awaits the panel's Settle() when the payload's Count is above 2, writes Watching into panel-note in an ElseIf when its Flag holds, and in its Else writes Kappa into the payload's WriteOnlyText; once its listeners return the panel shows its payload line.
